contracts.commit_point: conn.commit() immediately after cursor.execute inside each tool's confirmed branch: tools.py:94 (create_table), tools.py:116 (drop_table), tools.py:138 (update_records), tools.py:160 (insert_record), tools.py:182 (delete_records).
contracts.declared_mechanism: Per-tool code gate: each mutation tool checks 'if wrapper.context.human_confirmation:' before sqlite3.connect/cursor.execute/conn.commit and otherwise returns the refusal string. The flag lives on the shared RunContextWrapper[InputData] run context and, in the supplied files, is assigned only by the @function_tool ask_for_confirmation (human_in_the_loop.py), which prints a prompt, reads an interactive yes/no answer via input(), and sets wrapper.context.human_confirmation = True only for a case-insensitive 'yes' answer, False otherwise. ask_for_confirmation is registered on the same Agent tool list as the five mutation tools (sql_analyst.py:23), and DATA_ANALYST_INSTRUCTIONS mandate 'ALWAYS ask for human confirmation using the ask_for_confirmation tool' for any action that modifies the database (prompts.py:74).
contracts.forbidden_condition: cursor.execute of the mutating SQL statement followed by conn.commit() running while wrapper.context.human_confirmation is not True; in that state each tool must instead take its else branch and return the refusal message '❌ Human confirmation required. Please confirm the action.' without executing or committing anything.
pending_binding_information: The declared default value of human_confirmation in InputData (reviewers state it defaults to False) is unverifiable from supplied sources because cli_data_ai/agents/context/context.py was not provided.
The claim that ask_for_confirmation is the ONLY setter of human_confirmation is verified only within the supplied files; repository enumeration is incomplete, so other setters cannot be ruled out.
Whether the runtime resets human_confirmation between tool calls or after a successful mutation is not shown in the supplied source.
Whether the deployed runtime supplies the interactive stdin that ask_for_confirmation's input() prompt requires is not established by the supplied source.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution and commit of database-mutating SQL: CREATE TABLE via create_table(create_query), DROP TABLE IF EXISTS via drop_table(table_name), UPDATE via update_records(update_query), INSERT via insert_record(insert_query), and DELETE via delete_records(delete_query).
contracts.protected_resource: The SQLite database file {wrapper.context.database_name}.sqlite — its tables (schema) and records (rows) that the DDL/DML statements create, drop, update, insert, or delete.
contracts.protection_obligation: The SQLite mutation tools create_table, drop_table, update_records, insert_record, and delete_records must refuse to execute and commit their SQL DDL/DML against the target SQLite database unless wrapper.context.human_confirmation is True; within the supplied source that flag is assigned True only inside the ask_for_confirmation human-in-the-loop tool after an interactive yes/no answer, and DATA_ANALYST_INSTRUCTIONS require calling ask_for_confirmation before any database-modifying action. (Single merged obligation: the first- and second-phase reviewer opinions state the same requirement with duplicate wording.)
scope_limits: Obligation covers only the five dedicated mutation tools; the read tools sql_query_tool, describe_database, and profile_database contain no human_confirmation check, and sql_query_tool executes arbitrary agent-supplied SQL (tools.py:6-20) with no guard — whether that reaches an equivalent persisted effect is a runtime question not decided here.

human_confirmation is a persistent boolean on the shared run context; supplied source shows no reset of the flag after a mutation commits, so the gate is on flag state rather than on a fresh confirmation per action.
The prompts.py rules (including line 74) are prompt-level policy; the only code-level enforcement evidenced in the supplied source is the flag check inside each mutation tool.

The guard binds only effects on the SQLite file {wrapper.context.database_name}.sqlite; nothing in the supplied source extends it to other effects such as Metabase chart/dashboard creation by the dashboard agent.
Guard semantics (flag default value, alternative setters, reset/lifetime) depend on cli_data_ai/agents/context/context.py and the runner, neither of which is in the supplied source.
